stories.title: Air-stable, ultrathin superconductors developed for more scalable quantum devices
stories.desc: Super-thin superconducting materials, which are only one or a few atoms thick, have unique properties scientists can leverage to produce more compact, scalable, and efficient quantum devices. But these fragile materials degrade so rapidly in air that they are difficult to study or manufacture.

stories.title: New semiconductor maser operates continuously above room temperature
stories.desc: Lasers have become indispensable in everyday life and research, with applications ranging from data transmission and metrology to manufacturing. Masers, by contrast, have so far found hardly any practical applications.

stories.title: Attosecond X-ray method maps early electron motions that trigger chemical reactions
stories.desc: All chemistry starts with a push from electrons. In the early moments of a chemical reaction, it's the movement of electrons that initiates the breaking of old chemical bonds and forging of new ones, transforming one molecule into another.
